correctness.rationale: For every prime p, invariant probability mu has a canonical stationary two-sided digit extension. Its p-adic character at k/p^n depends exactly on n forward digits and, by stationary reversed-block equality, equals the nth truncation of the backward-digit real Fourier character. The omitted tail is at most p^-n, giving 2pi|k|p^-n. NonLebesgue reversed law has a nonzero Fourier coefficient; Lebesgue reversed law forces every finite digit block uniformly distributed and original mu Haar, including endpoint ambiguity because Lebesgue has zero atoms. The corresponding k/p^n escapes to infinity and obstructs all positive Fourier-decay exponents. Delta_-1 asymptotically saturates 2pi. value.rationale: The qualitative theorem fully classifies decay-eligible probabilities within a natural, highly nontrivial dynamical family (all shift-stationary p-adic digit laws), rather than only iid examples. The sharp boundary correspondence produces explicit spectral witnesses at arbitrarily high p-adic frequencies and an optimal universal finite-prefix error constant, informing the design of nonarchimedean Fourier-decaying measures and excluding stationary candidates. It does not rely on arbitrary parameter slices or a minor numerical improvement.
